messages.author: bfc2eb6b71169017
messages.subject: Re: Horizontal alignment of x-scale
parts:
This can be done using gridExtra::grid.arrange and ggplotGrob.
I took the liberty to edit your code to make it arguably easier to read. My suggestion here would be to adopt a more readable syntax writing style. Anything with spaces will do. :)

require(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)

start.ratio <- read.csv("../Downloads/start.ratio.csv", header = TRUE)
start.ratio$trunc_Start.ratio <- trunc(ymd_hms(start.ratio$Start.ratio),"days")

custom.breaks <- seq(20, 100, 20)

p1 <- ggplot(start.ratio[c(2,4,6,8,10), ], aes(x = Quantile, y = trunc_Start.ratio)) +
  xlab("") + 
  ylab("Start date of stratification") +
  geom_line(size = 0.7) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = custom.breaks) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.title.y = element_text(size = 20),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 20))

stra.ratio <- read.csv("../Downloads/stra.ratio.csv", header = TRUE)

p2 <- ggplot(stra.ratio[seq(2,10,2), ], aes(x = Quantile, y = stra.ratio)) +
  theme_bw() +
  xlab("Quantile of the wind speed(%)") + 
  ylab("Stratification ratio") +
  geom_line(size = 0.7) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = custom.breaks) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 20),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 20),
        plot.margin = unit(c(0.2, 0.1, 0.1, 0.48), "inches"),
        panel.grid = element_blank(), 
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 20, vjust = 10),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 20))

# As done by Baptiste on http://stackoverflow.com/a/13295880/322912
grid.arrange(rbind(ggplotGrob(p1), ggplotGrob(p2)))



​
